Here are the descriptions of the provided plots, following your guidelines:

The plots illustrate the relationship between sequence length and harmful refusal ratio for different vision-language models. Both plots share a common x-axis labeled “Sequence Length,” with a linear scale ranging from 128 to 1024, and tick labels at intervals of 128, 256, 512, and 1024. The y-axis is labeled “Harmful Refusal Ratio,” with a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 0.5, and tick labels at intervals of 0.1. 

The first plot displays four lines representing different models. A blue line, labeled “LlaVA-1.5-7B on FigStep,” begins at a value of 0.2 at a sequence length of 128, decreases to 0.18 at a sequence length of 256, rises to 0.22 at a sequence length of 512, and increases to 0.25 at a sequence length of 1024. An orange line, labeled “Qwen2-VL-7B on FigStep,” starts at 0.28 at a sequence length of 128, decreases to 0.23 at a sequence length of 256, rises to 0.32 at a sequence length of 512, and increases to 0.33 at a sequence length of 1024. A green line, labeled “LlaVA-1.5-7B on MMSafetyBench,” begins at 0.32 at a sequence length of 128, decreases to 0.26 at a sequence length of 256, remains at 0.26 at a sequence length of 512, and increases to 0.3 at a sequence length of 1024. A red line, labeled “Qwen2-VL-7B on MMSafetyBench,” starts at 0.35 at a sequence length of 128, decreases to 0.31 at a sequence length of 256, rises to 0.4 at a sequence length of 512, and increases to 0.44 at a sequence length of 1024.
